messages:
incident-bot: :pager: Pager alert: kv-cache-evictions-high on relayer-usw cluster (P1). Trigger: 3xx 429s spike over 5m. Paging oncall team. Runbook: https://redwood.grafana.net/runbooks/kv-eviction

jamie: saw it, I'm primary for USW today. jumping in. checking dashboards now.

alex: I'm secondary, can help with mitigations. tagging monitoring: grafana link?

jamie: grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/kv-cache?orgId=1  p95 token latency and eviction rate both spiking.

tariq: quick note — embedding routes have seen increased seq-lens which could bloat kv sizes. pushing a temporary route-redirect would reduce pressure.

jamie: good call. alex can you prepare the routing policy to shift embedding-heavy traffic to the fallback model pool (pool-emb-fallback-2)?

alex: on it. here's the policy snippet I'm about to apply:
```yaml
route: embed-heavy-fallback
match: request.path contains "/embeddings" and token_count > 1024
action: route_to pool-emb-fallback-2
priority: 50
```
apply in 2m unless objections.

monica: heads-up: one enterprise customer (acme-corp) reported timeouts, CX ticket #INC-4592. they saw ~30% failed requests on embeddings.

jamie: thanks. i'm opening a postmortem ticket and updating ACME status. assigning oncall notes.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step 1: validate evictions and memory pressure: `kubectl top pods -n relayer-usw`

jamie: ran checks: pod memory across batchers shows 78% usage, leader node showing continuous OOM-kick attempts in logs. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-14T10:12:03Z] evicting 1.2GB from kv-cache shard-7 (threshold exceeded)
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] p99 request latency spike -> 429
```

tariq: can we bump kv-cache eviction threshold or temporarily enable aggressive prefix caching to reduce churn? longer-term needs config change but we can toggle a config flag.

jamie: toggle prefix caching true for relayer-usw to reduce recompute. doing config change now: `rictl config set relayer-usw prefix_caching=true --ttl=30m`

alex: policy applied and routing active. monitoring for impact.

incident-bot: config change detected by deploy-bot: `rictl config set relayer-usw prefix_caching=true` initiated by jamie at 2026-03-14T10:16:05Z.

jamie: seeing eviction rate drop ~10% after toggle. 429 rate reduced from 18% -> 8% within 4m. still elevated but trending down.

monica: updating ACME ticket: posting workaround applied and ETA for full mitigation ~2h. pinging account team.

tariq: next action — scale relayer-usw batcher pool by +2 nodes (temporary) to smooth tail latency while we investigate root cause. I'm going to request capacity from Dedicated autoscale group.

alex: please include scaling command here so ops can audit: `rictl scale pool relayer-usw-batcher --add 2 --reason \"eviction-mitigation\"`

jamie: scaling request sent. dedicated autoscaler responded: queued, expected provisioning in ~6m.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step 4: if evictions persist after caching toggle and scale, consider rolling back the recent model quantization in canary (commit b4f23a) that started two days ago.

jamie: noted. check model commit in canary: `git rev-parse --short b4f23a` present on canary nodes. skipping rollback for now — monitor after scale.

incident-bot: customer-impact summary updated: ACME (enterprise) — degraded embeddings (30% errors) from 10:05–10:20 UTC; other customers — intermittent 429s, <5% traffic impacted.

monica: filed a short incident status to #customers-ops: "We observed embedding timeouts for ACME; temporary routing and cache tweaks applied; scaling in progress; next update in 30m."

alex: scale completed at 10:24 UTC. batcher pool up +2, memory usage distributed, eviction rate now down 60% from peak.

jamie: current status: degraded -> partial recovery. Key metrics: 429 rate 2.1% (was 18%), p95 latency back to acceptable range for non-embed routes, embeddings still ~4% errors.

tariq: actions remaining: deep-dive on why kv-cache grew (probable seq-len change + prefix invalidation), audit recent quantization config for canary, longer-term: increase kv shard memory for relayer-usw and add alerts for kv occupancy.

jamie: for handoff: i'm primary until 13:00 UTC; alex will be secondary until 12:30 then hand to monica. please monitor alerts: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts?filter=kv_eviction and keep incident channel updated.

monica: taking secondary at 12:30. leaving action items on the incident ticket.

alex: quick checklist for incoming shift:
- verify prefix_caching flag remains enabled
- confirm no new deploys touching relayer-usw model config
- run `rictl metrics query --expr=\"kv_evictions_total{cluster=\\\"relayer-usw\\\"}[5m]\"` every 15m for first hour

jamie: logged follow-ups in INC-4593:
- postmortem draft (owner: jamie)
- kv-shard-sizing proposal (owner: tariq)
- canary quantization audit (owner: alex)
- customer comms follow-up (owner: monica)

incident-bot: Incident updated to status: partial_recovery. P1 -> monitoring.

jamie: final for now — leaving detailed notes in the ticket and runbook links. handoff done. :wave:

monica: thanks team. will escalate if we see regression.

alex: cheers, all. I'll watch the dashboards for the next hour and then pass to monica.

sre-runbook-bot: Reminder: please attach the logs for leader node OOMs to the incident ticket and set `severity=service-impact` in the postmortem template.

jamie: attached logs and marked severity. handing off now.
